name: packfits
description: Airline carry-on, personal item and checked bag size rules from official sources, a bag fit check, a comparison across airlines, bags that fit, and theme park and cruise line bag rules.

interface.longDescription:
Will my carry-on fit? Is my backpack a personal item? How much is a checked bag? Packfits answers with each airline's own published rules, not guesses.

Airline bag rules: carry-on, personal item and checked bag limits in inches and centimeters, weight limits, typical bag fees and the fare caveats that catch travelers out, such as Basic Economy. Every rule links to the airline's official page and shows the date it was last checked.

Bag fit check: give your bag's outside size and Packfits tells you whether it fits, is just over the limit, or is too big. Bags can be turned to fit the sizer and soft-sided bags get a little leeway, the same way the packfits.com checker works.

Compare airlines: ask "what is the standard carry-on size?" and get every covered airline's limit from smallest to largest, plus the most common size, or learn which airlines your bag fits.

Bags that fit: ask for a carry-on or personal item that fits an airline, or have a bag that does not, and Packfits lists bags from its catalog that fit, with links to their Amazon product pages.

Theme parks: official rules for bag size, prohibited items, outside food and drink, lockers and strollers at 12 parks, including Disney World, Disneyland, Universal Orlando, Six Flags and Cedar Point.

Cruise lines: prohibited items, luggage, dress code and what the stateroom provides on 10 lines, including Royal Caribbean, Carnival, Norwegian, Disney Cruise Line and Princess.

Airlines covered: Delta, United, American, Southwest, Alaska, JetBlue, Frontier, Allegiant, Ryanair and Lufthansa.

No account or sign-in. Packfits only reads its own published data and never asks for personal information. Packfits earns a commission from qualifying Amazon purchases.
capabilities: Airline carry-on, personal item and checked bag size rules
Check whether a bag fits an airline's limit
Compare bag size limits across airlines
Find bags that fit an airline's limit
Theme park bag, food and locker rules
Cruise line packing rules and dress codes
defaultPrompt: Will my 22 x 14 x 9 inch carry-on fit on United?
What is the standard personal item size?
Can you bring food into Disney World?

positive.prompt: How big can a carry-on be on United?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives United's carry-on limit of 22 x 14 x 9 in (55.9 x 35.6 x 22.9 cm), with the personal item and checked bag limits, and cites the official united.com page and its check date.

positive.prompt: Will my 22 x 14 x 9 inch carry-on fit on American Airlines?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers that the bag fits American's 22 x 14 x 9 in carry-on limit, and suggests no bags.

positive.description: A question that names no airline
positive.prompt: What is the standard personal item size?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the most common personal item limit, 18 x 14 x 8 in, and lists every covered airline's limit from smallest to largest with official sources.

positive.prompt: Which bag should I buy to fit Ryanair's free personal item?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives Ryanair's 40 x 30 x 20 cm limit and lists catalog bags that fit it, with sizes and links to Amazon product pages, and notes the commission.

positive.prompt: Can you bring food into Disney World?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains that outside food and nonalcoholic drinks are allowed for personal use if they need no heating or temperature control, that glass containers are not allowed, and cites Disney's official page.

negative.description: Flight search is out of scope
negative.prompt: Find me a cheap flight from Austin to Chicago next week.

negative.description: Booking actions are out of scope
negative.prompt: Check me in for my Delta flight tomorrow.
Pay the checked bag fee for my Southwest flight.

review.commerce_description: Packfits does not sell products or process payments. When the user asks for a bag, or the user's bag does not fit, it lists bags from its catalog with links to their Amazon product pages, never to a cart or checkout. Those links carry Packfits' Amazon Associates tag, and every result that includes them states that Packfits earns a commission.

publication.release_notes: First release: bag size rules for 10 airlines with official sources, a fit check for any bag, a comparison across airlines, bags that fit an airline, and the published rules of 12 theme parks and 10 cruise lines.
